Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. ## What this changes Adds an optional Auto Review tool that captures sandbox changes and runs a restricted, caller-authorized reviewer on the host. **Example:** A sandbox session calls autoreview with {"mode":"local"}. - **Before:** The plugin cannot bind review execution to the prepared sandbox and original caller authority. - **After:** The installed helper captures sandbox changes, the host runs the permitted reviewer, and the helper returns a complete validated report. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Coherent optional feature with shipped-entry-point evidence, a resolved authority-proof gap, compatible additive contracts, and no open findings. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): Supplied guest execution exercises protected sandbox capture, helper defaults, model denial, concurrent reviews, and Stop cleanup; the real plugin/helper/native-CLI provider control records one allowed request and zero requests after model-policy revocation, resolving the prior rank-up request. | | **Patch quality** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Sandbox changes need review without substituting host Git state or exposing host credentials and tools. **Reason:** Maintainer-authored direction delivers a concrete checkpoint through an optional plugin and narrow generic capabilities. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** This maintainer-authored PR adds a useful sandbox review capability; no actionable introduced defects remain in this review. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `5f6e79d2fb40889cf0ac077a2fde09dc882138c1` ## Before merge None. ## Findings None.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The plugin connects the sandbox-owned review helper to host-native inference, carrying caller authority and returning complete reports through existing tool-result delivery. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Sandbox session] --> B[Auto Review plugin] B --> C[Protected sandbox helper] C --> D[Captured review request] D --> E[Caller model authority] E --> F[Restricted native reviewer] F --> C C --> G[Validated report] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Land the optional plugin with the merged native prerequisites and current canonical helper while retaining existing authority and result-delivery owners. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? This is a capability addition; source inspection confirms the missing sandbox-bound execution contract, and supplied guest runs exercise the added flow. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The implementation fits the existing plugin, sandbox, model-policy, native CLI, and canonical-helper owners without introducing a competing review engine or persistent job service. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [d6687fdf5fde](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d6687fdf5fde222def02b210b1acbf0e38b34944). ### Provenance checked - `Plugin invocation authority` keeps the original intent (861f60e0bc5c6ef585319db960d5b8ead190c4c7: Keep retained plugin effects bound to current invocation and plugin lifecycle authority.) - `Prepared native tool context` keeps the original intent (ddcae5101d781c68de156ce5013c0778090bee64: Carry prepared execution facts through asynchronous tool construction while preserving live checks.) - `Code Mode result projection and scheduling` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159359: Preserve nested-tool error messages in projected values; sequential-tool scheduling remains owned by the shared runtime.) - `Sandbox mount interpretation` keeps the original intent (0ab1513aaedf83db66fab68693de1ee6dffe0a3f: Keep filesystem tools aligned with overlapping mounts and protected resource precedence.) ### Testing Proof path: shipped entry point. ### Security None. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Introduced execution boundary:** The pinned introduced diff binds helper requests to caller model admission, fixes the host CLI entry, clears reviewer tools and ambient context, and preserves helper-owned report validation. ([`extensions/autoreview/src/tool.ts:336`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5f6e79d2fb40889cf0ac077a2fde09dc882138c1/extensions/autoreview/src/tool.ts#L336), [5f6e79d2fb40](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5f6e79d2fb40889cf0ac077a2fde09dc882138c1)) - **Updated authority proof resolves prior request:** The current body records an allowed production-path review making one synthetic HTTP provider request and a revoked-model control making zero requests after prompt handoff and native startup, with processes, exchanges, temporary state, and subscriptions settled. ([5f6e79d2fb40](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5f6e79d2fb40889cf0ac077a2fde09dc882138c1)) - **Protected installation and lifecycle ownership:** Capabilities retain the original invocation and plugin lifecycle; protected helper selection rejects workspace shadows, writable aliases, replacing overlays, and backends without enforced read-only resources. The merged helper change at https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/328 supplies admitted-model handoff, response ownership, terminal-model validation, and effective-model receipts; these responsibilities remain upstream.
